items.title: How AI and Autonomous Aircraft Are Changing Warfare
items.title_ko: How AI and Autonomous Aircraft Are Changing Warfare
items.summary_ko: Gary Steele, CEO, Shield AI, discusses how AI-piloted aircraft and autonomous drones are changing modern warfare and the balance of military power with Bloomberg’s Tom Giles at Bloomberg Tech 2026 in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Dan Ives Sees Anthropic IPO Facing Valuation Pressure
items.title_ko: Dan Ives Sees Anthropic IPO Facing Valuation Pressure
items.summary_ko: Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., discusses concerns about Anthropic’s upcoming IPO. He examines capital raised by hyperscalers, calling it the “start of winners and losers” in the AI trade and says chip stocks have about another 10% - 12% to fall.

items.title: Can Europe Build AI Sovereignty at Scale?
items.title_ko: Can Europe Build AI Sovereignty at Scale?
items.summary_ko: Suzanne Ashman, Managing Partner, Sovereign AI Fund and Johan Bergqvist, Chief Financial Officer, Mistral, discuss which parts of the AI stack Europe must control, where partnerships matter and how the region can build resilience with Bloomberg's Mark Bergen at Bloomberg Tech 2026 in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: AMD Needs a Huge Outlook to Avoid Intel’s Fate as AI Fears Rise
items.title_ko: AMD Needs a Huge Outlook to Avoid Intel’s Fate as AI Fears Rise
items.summary_ko: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. is one of this year’s best-performing chip stocks, but with skepticism about artificial-intelligence spending on the rise, it could use strong results and an aggressive outlook to maintain the momentum when the firm reports earnings Tuesday afternoon.

items.title: Palantir Is Concerned About Europe's Slow AI Adoption
items.title_ko: Palantir Is Concerned About Europe's Slow AI Adoption
items.summary_ko: Louis Mosley, who oversees Palantir's business in the UK and Europe, says, “blue chips on this side of the Atlantic are not yet adopting AI." He made the comments in a conversation with Tom Giles at Bloomberg Tech in London. "That worries me because we’re starting to see extraordinary results from those customers, those big American blue chips,” he adds.
